newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ACCC says telecom fees to drop 35 pct.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ACCC says telecom fees to drop 35 pct.

text.p: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said on Wednesday that prices of interconnection with Telstra Corp Ltd's main network have been reduced by 35 percent from July 1, 1997.

The ACCC, which will become the telecom industry watchdog once the market is deregulated from July 1, said the new price affirms the reduction in usage charges for interconnection detailed in a draft report earlier this month.

"The determination (ACCC ruling) should not be seen as mandating prices for all players, nor should it be seen as dictating interconnect prices over the long term," ACCC commissioner Rod Shogren said in a statement.
"Access pricing outcomes will most likely be primarily determined through commercial negotiations in the long-term," he said.
Shrogen said this price does not imply that all access seekers should pay the same price for interconnection in the future.
ACCC said the main usage charges for interconnection have been reduced for capital cities to 2.84 cents a minute in peak periods and to 1.34 cents per minute in off-peak periods.
These charges are a slight increase on the usage charges specified in the draft determination based on some revisions in light of further information, the commission said.
Currently a number of service providers and Optus Communications Pty Ltd connect to the Telstra network.

ACCC said it has also recommended an unspecified reduction in the charges service providers must pay for non-code access, which allows customers to select a service provider without the necessity to dial an override code.
"This determination will encourage competition in the provision of telecommunications services by allowing new players to compete effectively with existing carriers," Shogren said.
"This is likely to benefit consumers through lower prices and improved service quality," he said.
Optus is 25 percent owned by Mayne Nickless Ltd, 24.5 percent each owned by Cable and Wireless Plc and BellSouth Corp. The rest is owned by local investors.
